Once upon a time three Billy Goats lived on a hill.
Their name was Gruff.
Little Billy was the smallest, Middle Billy was a bit bigger, and Big Billy was the biggest of all.
The grass on their hill was getting short.
Across the river there was a meadow full of sweet green grass.
To get to the meadow, the goats had to cross a wooden bridge.
And under the bridge lived a grumpy Troll, with eyes like saucers and a nose as long as a carrot.
Little Billy went first.
Trip, trap, trip, trap, went his little hooves on the bridge.
Who is that trip-trapping over my bridge?
said Troll.
It is only I, Little Billy Goat Gruff,
said Little Billy in a tiny voice.
I am going to the meadow to eat grass.
Nobody crosses my bridge without a fuss!
Oh, please let me cross,
said Little Billy.
I am so small.
Wait for my brother, who is much bigger than I.
Well, be off with you,
And Little Billy skipped across the bridge to the meadow.
Then Middle Billy came.
Trip, trap, trip, trap, went his hooves on the bridge.
It is only I, Middle Billy Goat Gruff,
said Middle Billy.
Very well, be off with you,
And Middle Billy trotted across the bridge to the meadow.
At last Big Billy came.
TRIP, TRAP, TRIP, TRAP, went his big hooves on the bridge.
It is I, Big Billy Goat Gruff,
said Big Billy in a deep, loud voice.
said Troll, and he stamped onto the bridge.
Why are you so grumpy?
said Big Billy.
I think you are just lonely.
Come across with us and taste the sweet green grass.
Nobody ever asks me to come along,
He nibbled a little grass, and it was so good that he smiled for the very first time.
Big Billy and the Troll crossed the bridge to join the other goats in the meadow.
The three Billy Goats Gruff and their new friend ate sweet green grass all summer long, and they grew so fat that they could hardly walk home.
Snip, snap, snout, this tale's told out.
